title: Total quiescent supply current of the untrimmed core over the full PVT matrix
claim: README.md 'Target specification (ratified -- see DR-005, issue #1)' row 'Iq' (< 50 uA), for the 3.3 V primary flavor (DR-001). Measures the total current out of the single supply source feeding design/bandgap_core.sch (both core branches, the R2A/R2B legs and the error amplifier's mirrored tail), open-circuit at VREF, over the full 45-point PVT matrix.

measurements.name: iq
measurements.note: Total quiescent supply current. Upper limit is DR-005's ratified < 50 uA target column (the < 20 uA stretch column is out of scope for wave 1 per DR-001's scope note). The 1 uA lower bound is a liveness floor, not a spec line: it is the second half of the degenerate-state guard, because the all-off solution draws essentially nothing and would otherwise pass the upper limit trivially.

measurements.name: vref
measurements.note: Degenerate-state guard, not the accuracy claim: a deliberately wide band that only asserts the core was up and regulating when Iq was read. The +/-2% output-accuracy claim is sim/output-voltage-tc/'s.

measurements.name: vgdrv
measurements.note: Degenerate-state guard on the PMOS mirror gate. In the all-off solution this node parks at VDD, which is at least 2.97 V anywhere in the supply range, so an upper bound of 2.9 V excludes that state at every corner instead of silently reporting a plausible-looking near-zero current.

spread_checks.note: Iq must move by at least 1 uA across the 45-point matrix. A dead-flat current would mean the corner/temperature/supply knobs are not reaching the simulator -- the same liveness argument sim/pdk-smoke/ makes for the harness itself.

notes: Full 45-point PVT matrix, no subset: an operating point is cheap and Iq is meaningful at every individual corner, unlike the box-TC and line-regulation claims whose benches sweep one axis internally.

Solver tolerances are tightened well past ngspice's defaults: reltol=1e-6 (default 1e-3), vntol=1e-9 (default 1e-6), abstol=1e-15 (default 1e-12). This is a MEASUREMENT-RESOLUTION requirement, not a taste preference. At the default reltol=1e-3 the DC solver is only obliged to converge a ~1.175 V node to ~1.2 mV, and the first run of sim/line-regulation/ (record 20260803-100723-77b96e3) duly reported a 0.11 .. 1.27 mV supply-induced output shift that, on inspection of the raw sweep, was non-monotonic point-to-point jitter at exactly that amplitude -- i.e. the solver's convergence noise floor, not a property of the circuit. Re-run with these tolerances the same sweep is smooth and monotone with a shallow minimum near 3.45 V, and the shift drops to tens of microvolts. Every DC-based bench in this suite shares the setting so that all four are read off the same, resolved operating point.
